item.text:
## 2B.9 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** **No clear accountability.** In the 2024 South China Sea record, Marcos and his administration repeatedly **blamed China**, defended Philippine personnel as professional, and framed Philippine actions as restrained and lawful. I did **not** find a credible instance where Marcos accepted responsibility for Philippine-side military failures, civilian harm, illegal conduct, or later evidence undermining his public justification. The evidence is mostly the opposite: rebuttal, attribution of blame to China, and de-escalation language.

| ID | Direction | Title / Publisher / Date / URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Limited favorable / restraint | [Philippines not in business of instigating wars, says President Marcos](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/philippines-not-in-business-of-instigating-wars-says-president-marcos-3492819) - Reuters, 2024-06-23 | Marcos said the Philippines was not instigating wars and would settle disputes peacefully. This supports restraint, but it is not an admission of error or accountability for any Philippine-side conduct. | `2B.9`, `2B.6`, `2B.1` |
| E2 | Limited favorable / restraint | [Philippines says won't raise South China Sea tensions, won't use water cannons](https://theprint.in/world/philippines-says-wont-raise-south-china-sea-tensions-wont-use-water-cannons/2071484/) - Reuters, 2024-05-06 | Marcos said the Philippines would not use water cannons or offensive weapons and did not want to raise tensions. Again, this shows restraint, not responsibility-taking for earlier incidents. | `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.1` |
| E3 | Critical / no accountability | [Philippines rejects Chinese allegation that troops point guns at its coast guard](https://www.stripes.com/theaters/asia_pacific/2024-06-04/philippines-china-provocations-14073962.html) - Reuters, 2024-06-04 | When China alleged Philippine troops had pointed guns, the Philippine military rejected the allegation and said personnel acted under rules of engagement with professionalism. There is no sign of self-investigation or acceptance of fault. | `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.5` |

Marcos did not accept responsibility for the incident, and I found no later admission of Philippine fault. | `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.6` |
| E5 | Critical / no accountability | [Philippines accuses China of using 'illegal force' to deliberately disrupt resupply mission](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/philippines-accuses-china-of-using-illegal-force-to-deliberately-disrupt-resupply-mission-3491363) - Reuters, 2024-06-24 | After the June 17 clash injured a sailor, the Philippine defense chief said China used illegal force and that the incident was not a misunderstanding or accident. Marcos’s government used the incident to harden its criticism of China, not to acknowledge Philippine-side error. | `2B.9`, `2B.3`, `2B.6` |

That is condemnation of the other side, not accountability for Philippine conduct. | `2B.9`, `2B.6`, `2B.4` |

I found no admission of responsibility by Marcos or his government. | `2B.9`, `2B.6`, `2B.7` |
| E8 | Critical / no accountability | [Philippines says China's maritime-related proposals run contrary to its interests](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/philippines-says-chinas-maritimerelated-proposals-run-contrary-to-its-interests-3333337) - Reuters, 2024-03-12 | Marcos said China’s proposals on South China Sea management rested on a questionable premise and that it was difficult to see a way forward. This reflects bargaining, but not responsibility for Philippine conduct or a correction of earlier claims. | `2B.9`, `2B.7`, `2B.6` |

### Synthesis

- **What the record shows:** Marcos consistently framed Philippine actions as **professional, restrained, and lawful**, while attributing wrongdoing to China.
- **What it does not show:** I found **no credible 2024 example** of Marcos accepting blame for Philippine military failure, civilian harm, illegal conduct, or later contradictions to his stated justification.
- **Search gap:** The relevant incidents were mostly **maritime confrontations**, not formal military campaigns. So there was little opportunity for the kind of post-conflict accountability that this question usually captures, but the available record still does not show a clear acceptance of responsibility.

**Working judgment for 2B.9:** **No, not on the evidence found.** Marcos did **not** clearly accept accountability in 2024; he mainly **defended Philippine conduct and blamed China**.
